Source.ReleaseReview: Re-checked against the released v2.0.0 tag. Its migration file adds one row to the 2026-09-30 copy (MS.SHAREPOINT.3.3v1 to v2: the rule now also applies when the external sharing slider is set to Existing guests) and corrects several old-id descriptions and the range targets of MS.DEFENDER.1.2v1 to 1.5v1 (now MS.SECURITYSUITE.1.1v1 - MS.SECURITYSUITE.1.4v1; the 2026-09-30 copy read 1.4v2 to 1.4v5), which this file records as MigrationNewId; no current id NRG cites changed. The released baseline text of every rule NRG cites was compared with the text at commit df84e9d: the changes are editorial (wording, punctuation, admin center navigation) except MS.SECURITYSUITE.5.2v1, whose statement changed from the OMB M-21-31 minimum to "retained and searchable for a minimum of 3 months and retrievable for a minimum of 12 months" (the recorded notes already judge that text), and MS.TEAMS.4.1v1, whose instructions now also ask that the accepted SMTP domains list stay empty (see TMS-2.4). The 109 current policy ids in the released baselines equal Config/framework-baselines/scuba-ids-v2.0.0.txt.
Source.RuleVersions: Rule ids carry their own version suffix (v1, v2, v3); the current id is the one ScubaGear 2.0.0 emits. Where the migration file maps an old id to a range or to None, the mapping below was decided per requirement against the NRG evaluator.

Relations.Equivalent: The NRG evaluator checks the same requirement.
Relations.Partial: The NRG evaluator covers part of the requirement, or a stricter or looser form of it. Read the note.
Relations.Manual: The NRG control is manual or advisory; it asserts nothing about the rule.
Relations.Unsupported: The NRG control does not establish this requirement. The citation stays only where the current id still exists, flagged; an obsolete id with no equivalent was removed.

Mappings.Title: Legacy Authentication Blocked
Mappings.Note: Both require legacy authentication blocked for all users. SCuBA allows no user exclusions unless configured; NRG reports excluded accounts as an exception (Partial) when no other policy covers them.

Mappings.Title: MFA Required for All Users
Mappings.Note: v1 was renumbered to v2 in the migration file with the same requirement (MFA for all users). NRG also judges registration separately.

Mappings.Title: Phishing-Resistant MFA Required for Admins
Mappings.Note: SCuBA names its highly privileged roles; NRG compares against the privileged roles in this tenant's own role catalog.

Mappings.Title: Sign-in Risk CA Policy
Mappings.Note: SCuBA requires high-risk sign-ins to be blocked; NRG accepts a risk policy that blocks or requires remediation at high and medium risk.

Mappings.Title: User Risk CA Policy
Mappings.Note: SCuBA requires high-risk users to be blocked; NRG accepts a policy that blocks or requires password change.

Mappings.Title: Identity Protection Risky User Workflow
Mappings.Note: Notification on high-risk users; NRG checks the risky-user workflow.

Mappings.Title: Privileged Accounts Use Dedicated Cloud-Only Accounts
Mappings.Note: Privileged accounts are cloud-only and dedicated.

Mappings.Title: Device Code Authentication Flow Blocked
Mappings.Note: Device code flow blocked (for all users on all applications).

Mappings.Title: Users Without MFA — Named List
Mappings.Note: A named list of users without registered MFA is registration, not phishing-resistant enforcement (3.1).

Mappings.Title: OAuth Apps with Tenant-Wide Consent — Named List
Mappings.Note: A list of apps with tenant-wide consent is an inventory, not the user-consent restriction (5.2). Covered by AAD-6.2.

Mappings.Title: No Application Holds Tenant-Takeover Permissions
Mappings.Note: Application permissions held by apps are not the user-consent restriction (5.2).

Mappings.Title: Applications with Tenant-Wide Data Permissions — Named List
Mappings.Note: Application permissions held by apps are not the user-consent restriction (5.2).

Mappings.Title: Conditional Access Policies Deployed
Mappings.Note: Only the legacy-authentication track of AAD-2.1 overlaps MS.AAD.1.1; AAD-2.1 also judges MFA tracks and the approved policy set.

Mappings.Title: Device Compliance Enforced via CA
Mappings.Note: The baseline text asks for a compliant or hybrid-joined device. ScubaGear's automated check passes only a grant of exactly compliantDevice OR domainJoinedDevice; the NRG evaluator also credits a policy requiring a compliant device alone (it checks combined coverage, client app types and narrowing), so a tenant can pass here and fail ScubaGear's check. Reviewed 2026-10-26.

Mappings.Title: Global Administrator Count 2-4, Cloud-Only
Mappings.Note: Stricter than the rule: SCuBA allows two to eight Global Administrators, NRG (since baseline v1.1) two to four, as CIS 1.1.3 does. Every NRG pass meets SCuBA; a tenant with five to eight passes SCuBA and fails NRG.

Mappings.Title: No Permanent Admin Role Assignments
Mappings.Note: Re-cited 2026-10-27: MS.AAD.7.3v1 (cloud-only privileged accounts, AAD-10.2's requirement) was removed and MS.AAD.7.4v1 cited, the rule AAD-3.2 judges: no permanent active assignment to a highly privileged role. ScubaGear's check fails a role holding any active assignment with no end date, unless the principal is listed as an exemption in its configuration file, and requires Entra ID P2. Stricter: Satisfied also needs at least one PIM-eligible assignment, and every active assignment that is not a PIM activation counts as permanent, a time-bound one included (end dates are not read). Looser: service principals are not judged; NRG's 17-role list omits Hybrid Identity Administrator, one of ScubaGear's eight highly privileged roles; and cloud-only Global Administrators excluded from Conditional Access are set aside as emergency access accounts (the exception the rule's note allows) by that inference, not by an approved list. PIM not licensed is not assessed.

Mappings.Title: PIM GA Activation Requires Approval
Mappings.Note: Global Administrator activation requires approval.

Mappings.Title: Guest Invite Permissions Restricted
Mappings.Note: Only Guest Inviters can invite guests.

Mappings.Title: B2B Guest Default Permissions Restricted
Mappings.Note: Guest directory access limited.

Mappings.Title: User App Registration Disabled
Mappings.Note: Only administrators register applications.

Mappings.Title: User Consent to Apps Restricted
Mappings.Note: Both require user consent to applications restricted. The admin consent workflow is the separate rule MS.AAD.5.3 (AAD-6.3) and is not part of this verdict.

Mappings.Title: Admin Consent Workflow Enabled
Mappings.Note: Admin consent workflow configured.

Mappings.Title: PIM Alerts Configured
Mappings.Note: NRG cannot read PIM alert configuration; the control is manual.

Mappings.Title: Authenticator Number Matching Enabled
Mappings.Note: v2 requires login context information. NRG's control is number matching, which Microsoft enforces for every Authenticator push notification since May 2023; the control is recorded as enforced by the platform and not scored. The additional-context setting the v2 policy requires is collected (AdditionalContextFeatureState) and not scored.

Mappings.Title: Passwordless Authentication Methods Available
Mappings.Note: MS.AAD.3.1 requires phishing-resistant MFA ENFORCED for all users; AAD-9.2 only checks that passwordless methods are available. Enforcement is AAD-1.3 (administrators).

Mappings.Title: Safe Attachments Enabled with Block Action
Mappings.Note: The migration maps the old preset rule to a range (1.1 to 1.4). Safe Attachments with a block action overlaps "malware is quarantined or dropped" (1.3) only.

Mappings.Title: Safe Links Enabled and Hardened
Mappings.Note: NRG is stricter in scope. SCuBA 7.1 passes when the Standard or Strict preset applies URL block-list comparison; NRG also judges recipients covered only by the built-in protection policy (click-through allowed, URL rewrite off) and reports them as not protected. Safe Links hardening overlaps URL block-list comparison (7.1); SCuBA 7.2 and 7.3 (download scanning, click tracking) are separate rules.

Mappings.Title: Spoof Intelligence Enabled
Mappings.Note: SCuBA 2.0 has no rule for spoof intelligence; the migrated range does not cover it. Obsolete reference removed; the NRG control stays.

Mappings.Title: Preset Security Policies Applied
Mappings.Note: SCuBA 2.0 judges the outcomes (attachment blocking, scanning, quarantine), not whether the Standard or Strict preset is enabled. Obsolete reference removed; the NRG control stays.

Mappings.Title: Zero-Hour Auto Purge Enabled
Mappings.Note: Zero-hour auto purge is how mail is reviewed after delivery (1.2); SCuBA states the capability, NRG verifies the setting for spam, phishing and malware.

Mappings.Title: Anti-Malware Common Attachments Blocked
Mappings.Note: SCuBA requires click-to-run attachments (at minimum .exe, .cmd, .vbe) blocked. NRG verifies the attachment filter and, once approved, the blocked-type list.

Mappings.Title: High Confidence Spam to Quarantine
Mappings.Note: High-confidence spam to quarantine overlaps "spam and phishing are not delivered to the inbox" (6.1).

Mappings.Title: Bulk Mail Threshold Configured
Mappings.Note: SCuBA 2.0 has no bulk-mail threshold rule. Obsolete reference removed; the NRG control stays.

Mappings.Title: Defender Alert Email Notifications Configured
Mappings.Note: Alerts sent to a monitored address: NRG judges recipients and, once configured, the NRG monitoring address.

Mappings.Title: DLP Policy Covers All Key Workloads
Mappings.Note: ScubaGear 3.2 is met only when ONE enabled rule, in an Enable-mode policy, matches all three of SSN, ITIN and Credit Card Number, and that policy's location is All for each of Exchange, OneDrive, SharePoint, Teams and Devices. NRG judges workload coverage: enforcing policies with whole-workload scope whose rules match sensitive information types, whatever the types. Policies can cover every workload and still fail 3.2 when no single rule matches all three named types.

Mappings.Title: DLP Policy Uses Sensitive Information Types
Mappings.Note: SCuBA requires the policy to block named types (card numbers, ITIN, SSN and others); NRG verifies detection of sensitive information types in enforcing rules and reports blocking only when read.

Mappings.Title: Risky OAuth Application Alerts Configured
Mappings.Note: Risky OAuth alerts are not among the alerts SCuBA 4.1 requires. Obsolete reference removed; the NRG control stays.

Mappings.Title: Priority Accounts Tagged in Defender
Mappings.Note: A priority-account tag is not impersonation protection (SCuBA 2.1). Obsolete reference removed; the NRG control stays (manual).

Mappings.Title: Endpoint DLP Policy Active on Managed Devices
Mappings.Note: Devices are one of the locations SCuBA 3.2 lists, and 3.2 also needs one enabled rule matching SSN, ITIN and Credit Card Number; NRG DEF-4.5 checks that endpoint DLP policies are active on managed devices.

Mappings.Title: Safe Links Protects Office Applications
Mappings.Note: Safe Links for Office applications overlaps URL block-list comparison (7.1) in Office documents.

Mappings.Title: SPF Record Published
Mappings.Note: v3 accepts a hard or soft fail and is the current rule; NRG judges that an SPF record is published and its policy ending.

Mappings.Title: DKIM Records Published
Mappings.Note: NRG verifies the published selector records; SCuBA verifies DKIM is enabled in Exchange Online for each domain.

Mappings.Title: DMARC Policy at Quarantine or Reject
Mappings.Note: SCuBA requires p=reject. The NRG baseline accepts p=quarantine or p=reject. Same configuration, two standards: report the observed policy and judge each against its own requirement.

Mappings.Title: Mailbox Audit Logging Enabled
Mappings.Note: Mailbox auditing enabled; NRG also checks the audit bypass list.

Mappings.Title: SMTP Client Authentication Disabled
Mappings.Note: SMTP AUTH disabled.

Mappings.Title: External Auto-Forwarding Blocked
Mappings.Note: SCuBA reads the remote-domain automatic-forwarding setting (allowed domains configurable). NRG reads outbound spam policies and remote domains and has no allowed-domain list.

Mappings.Title: DKIM Signing Enabled for All Domains
Mappings.Note: NRG is stricter. SCuBA 3.1 passes when DKIM signing is enabled; NRG also requires a 2048-bit key and reports a domain with a 1024-bit key as Partial. A pass here with an NRG Partial is expected, not a disagreement.

Mappings.Title: Anti-Phishing Impersonation Protection Enabled
Mappings.Note: SCuBA requires impersonation protection for a sensitive-user list. NRG verifies domain and mailbox-intelligence protection and judges approved priority users only when NRG approves a list (Config/tp-standards.json).

Mappings.Title: Alert Policy — Email Forwarding Rules
Mappings.Note: SCuBA lists required alerts (suspicious sending, connector, forwarding); NRG checks the forwarding-rule alert only.

Mappings.Title: Alert Policy — Unusual Mail Volume
Mappings.Note: Unusual mail volume overlaps suspicious email sending patterns (4.1 a).

Mappings.Title: Transport Rules Changes Audited
Mappings.Note: Transport-rule change auditing is not unified audit logging (5.1). Obsolete reference removed; the NRG control stays.

Mappings.Title: Mailbox Audit Log Age Limit Sufficient
Mappings.Note: Re-cited 2026-10-26 after the evaluator stopped passing when custom audit retention policies were not read: Satisfied requires Exchange audit records to stay searchable for at least 90 days, with every Exchange-scoped custom audit retention policy read; covers the 'searchable for 3 months' half of 5.2 for Exchange record types only. The 12-month retrievability half and other record types are not checked here (PVW-4.2 checks one-year retention). The 2026-09-30 review had removed the old MS.DEFENDER.6.3v1 reference because the evaluator then read AuditLogAgeLimit.

Mappings.Title: Admin Audit Log Enabled
Mappings.Note: Admin audit log enabled overlaps unified audit logging (5.1); NRG judges searchability separately.

Mappings.Title: Safe Attachments for SharePoint OneDrive Teams Enabled
Mappings.Note: Safe Attachments for SharePoint, OneDrive and Teams = attachments in those workloads scanned for malware.

Mappings.Title: Anti-Spam Inbound Policy Properly Configured
Mappings.Note: SCuBA 2.0 has no rule for the anti-spam inbound policy settings NRG checks. Obsolete reference removed; the NRG control stays.

Mappings.Title: Per-User Mailbox Audit Logging Enabled for All Mailboxes
Mappings.Note: Per-user mailbox auditing; SCuBA states the tenant requirement.

Mappings.Title: Priority Account Protection Active in Anti-Phishing Policy
Mappings.Note: Priority-account protection in the anti-phishing policy overlaps sensitive-user impersonation protection (2.1).

Mappings.Title: Mailboxes with External Email Forwarding — Named List
Mappings.Note: Mailbox-level forwarding is not the remote-domain forwarding setting SCuBA reads.

Mappings.Title: Mailboxes with Audit Logging Disabled — Named List
Mappings.Note: Named mailboxes with auditing bypassed; SCuBA states the tenant requirement.

Mappings.Title: Per-User SMTP AUTH Override — Named List
Mappings.Note: Per-user SMTP AUTH overrides versus tenant SMTP AUTH disabled.

Mappings.Title: No Mailbox Forwarding to External Addresses
Mappings.Note: Mailbox forwarding is not the remote-domain forwarding setting SCuBA reads.

Mappings.Title: No Inbox Rules Forwarding Externally
Mappings.Note: Inbox-rule forwarding is not the remote-domain forwarding setting SCuBA reads.

Mappings.Title: No Mailboxes with Per-User Audit Explicitly Disabled
Mappings.Note: Per-user audit bypass versus tenant mailbox auditing.

Mappings.Title: No Per-User SMTP AUTH Overrides
Mappings.Note: Per-user SMTP AUTH overrides versus tenant SMTP AUTH disabled.

Mappings.Title: Power Platform Tenant Isolation Enabled
Mappings.Note: Tenant isolation enabled. The released v2.0.0 baseline marks the rule SHALL (last modified April 2026) and CISA lists it as a BOD 25-01 required configuration. (The 2026-09-30 ScubaGear run reported this rule as "test results missing".)

Mappings.Title: Power Platform DLP Policy Active
Mappings.Note: SCuBA requires a DLP policy restricting connectors in the default environment; NRG checks that a DLP policy is active.

Mappings.Title: Power Platform Environment Creation Restricted
Mappings.Note: Environment creation restricted to admins.

Mappings.Title: Power Platform Connector Classification Reviewed
Mappings.Note: Connector classification review versus a DLP policy restricting the default environment.

Mappings.Title: Power Automate Governance Policy Active
Mappings.Note: No documented setting; the NRG control requires manual verification.

Mappings.Title: Power Apps Portal Creation Restricted
Mappings.Note: Power Pages site creation restricted; NRG reads the tenant setting when returned.

Mappings.Title: Audit Log Retention Minimum 90 Days
Mappings.Note: SCuBA requires 3 months searchable and 12 months retrievable; NRG checks a 90-day minimum and (PVW-4.2) one year.

Mappings.Title: Audit Logs Exported to SIEM
Mappings.Note: SIEM export is not readable from Microsoft 365; the NRG control is manual.

Mappings.Title: Microsoft Purview Audit (Premium) Enabled
Mappings.Note: Reviewed 2026-10-26: PVW-4.1 now scores Satisfied only when UnifiedAuditLogIngestionEnabled = True is read from the Exchange Online session, the setting 5.1 audits, beside Audit (Premium) licensing for every licensed member user; so every pass meets 5.1 and the control is stricter. PVW-1.1 remains the direct unified-audit-log control.

Mappings.Title: Audit Log Retention Policy Extends to 1 Year or More
Mappings.Note: Retention to one year overlaps "retrievable for 12 months" (5.2).

Mappings.Title: External Sharing Restricted
Mappings.Note: External sharing limited to existing guests or organization only.

Mappings.Title: Default Sharing Link Not Anonymous
Mappings.Note: SCuBA requires the default link to be "Specific people"; NRG requires it not to be anonymous.

Mappings.Title: External Sharing Link Expiration Configured
Mappings.Note: Anyone-link expiry of 30 days or less. Needs the SharePoint shell.

Mappings.Title: Reauthentication Required for Sharing Links
Mappings.Note: Checked 2026-10-27 against the released v2 text ("Reauthentication days for people who use a verification code SHALL be set to 30 days or less"; v2 also applies when the sharing slider is Existing guests). SPO-2.7 reads the verification-code reauthentication setting (EmailAttestationRequired and EmailAttestationReAuthDays, SharePoint shell) and judges it for every sharing level except "Only people in your organization", so the Existing guests case is judged. Stricter than the rule: Satisfied needs 15 days or fewer (CIS 7.2.10), so every NRG pass meets v2, while 16 to 30 days is an NRG Partial that meets v2. Not assessed without the SharePoint shell.

Mappings.Title: External Federation Access Restricted
Mappings.Note: External access per-domain only.

Mappings.Title: External Participants Cannot Take Screen Control
Mappings.Note: External participants cannot request control.

Mappings.Title: Unverified App Publisher Blocked
Mappings.Note: SCuBA: only agency-approved third-party apps; NRG: unverified publishers blocked.

Mappings.Title: Teams Email Integration Disabled
Mappings.Note: Teams email integration disabled (AllowEmailIntoChannel = False), the setting ScubaGear's automated check reads. The v2.0.0 implementation steps also ask that the "Accept channel email from these SMTP domains" list stay empty; neither ScubaGear's check nor NRG reads that list, a list that limits which domains may send to a channel and so matters only while email into channels is allowed.

Mappings.Title: External User Chat Restricted
Mappings.Note: SCuBA: internal users should not initiate contact with unmanaged users; NRG: external user chat restricted.

Mappings.Title: PSTN Users Cannot Bypass Lobby
Mappings.Note: Dial-in users cannot bypass the lobby.

Mappings.Title: Auto-Admit Only Authenticated Organization Users
Mappings.Note: SCuBA: anonymous and dial-in callers not admitted automatically; NRG: auto-admit only organization users.

Mappings.Title: Anonymous Users Cannot Start Meetings
Mappings.Note: Anonymous users cannot start meetings.

Mappings.Title: Teams External Domain Federation Restricted to Allowlist
Mappings.Note: External federation restricted to allowed domains.

Mappings.Title: Phishing Directed to Quarantine Not Junk
Mappings.Note: Added 2026-10-26: phishing directed to quarantine in every policy in force covers the phishing half of "spam and phishing are not delivered to the inbox" (6.1), the same basis on which DEF-2.5 cites it for high-confidence spam.

Mappings.Title: Non-Compliant Device Access Blocked via CA
Mappings.Note: Added 2026-10-26: the same judgment as AAD-2.3 (Get-TPCADeviceComplianceCoverage). ScubaGear's automated check passes only a grant of exactly compliantDevice OR domainJoinedDevice; a compliant-only policy passes here and fails that check.

Mappings.Title: Application Credentials Current and Short-Lived
Mappings.Note: Added 2026-10-26: Satisfied requires the enabled default application management policy to restrict passwordLifetime to 180 days or less with no exempted actors or created-after date, which is 5.6. It also restricts asymmetricKeyLifetime to 180 days, stricter than MS.AAD.5.7v1's 365, which is met but not cited (one ScubaGear rule per control).

Mappings.Title: SMS and Voice Call Authentication Methods Disabled
Mappings.Note: Added 2026-10-27. The v2 rule requires SMS, voice call and email OTP disabled; ScubaGear reads the Sms, Voice and Email method states in the authentication methods policy. AAD-17.3 judges the same policy's Sms and Voice states (Satisfied only when both read disabled); Email OTP is AAD-17.5's half, so each control covers part of the rule.

Mappings.Title: Email OTP Authentication Method Disabled
Mappings.Note: Added 2026-10-27. Covers the email OTP third of the v2 rule (Email method state disabled in the authentication methods policy, the setting ScubaGear reads); SMS and voice call are AAD-17.3's part.

Mappings.Title: Passwords Set to Never Expire
Mappings.Note: Added 2026-10-27. Both read each domain's passwordValidityPeriodInDays. Stricter than ScubaGear's check, so every NRG pass meets the rule: NRG requires 2147483647 on every verified domain, federated and subdomains included, and reads an unset value as Microsoft's 90-day default (a shortfall), while ScubaGear judges managed verified domains only, takes a subdomain's value from its root, and accepts an unset value (null) as never expiring, which its v2.0.0 instructions say Microsoft treats as never expire for tenants created after October 2021. A tenant whose domains read null therefore passes ScubaGear and is an NRG shortfall: report both.

Mappings.Title: External Calendar Sharing Not Available
Mappings.Note: Added 2026-10-27. Stricter than the rule, which lets calendar details be shared with specific domains: Satisfied needs the default sharing policy disabled outright and no other enabled sharing policy sharing calendars with every domain (*) or anonymously, so every pass meets the rule. It differs from ScubaGear's automated check, which fails any sharing policy whose domain entries name * with a calendar action whether or not the policy is enabled: a disabled default policy that still lists *:CalendarSharingFreeBusySimple is an NRG pass and a ScubaGear failure. Contacts sharing (MS.EXO.6.1v1) is not checked by any NRG control.

Mappings.Title: OneDrive Content Sharing Restricted
Mappings.Note: Added 2026-10-27. Same setting (OneDriveSharingCapability). Stricter: Satisfied needs Only people in your organization (Disabled, or SharePoint external sharing off, which OneDrive cannot exceed), while the rule also accepts Existing guests, which NRG scores Partial (CIS 7.2.4). Every NRG pass meets the rule. Not assessed without the SharePoint shell unless SharePoint sharing is off.

Mappings.Title: SharePoint External Sharing Limited to Allowed Domains
Mappings.Note: Added 2026-10-27. Covers the approved-domain half, the setting ScubaGear's automated check reads (sharing domain restriction mode set to the allow list, not applicable when sharing is limited to the organization). Stricter: the allow list must name at least one domain. The rule's approved-security-group alternative is not credited here (SPO-5.6 reads the security group allow list, and ScubaGear does not check it), so a tenant restricting sharing by security group alone is an NRG Gap.

Mappings.Title: SharePoint Default Sharing Link Permission Is View
Mappings.Note: Added 2026-10-27. Default sharing link permission View (DefaultLinkPermission, the setting ScubaGear reads). Needs the SharePoint shell. MS.SHAREPOINT.3.2v1 (the permissions Anyone links may grant, FileAnonymousLinkType and FolderAnonymousLinkType) is a different setting and is not checked.
